q: Tell me about a time you handled a scope change from a client.
a: Use situation-action-result: restate the need, quantify the impact on time/cost/risk, offer options with a recommendation, get the decision in writing, update the plan. Give the outcome and what you learned.
followUps: What would you do if they insisted on everything?

q: A clinic gets hundreds of WhatsApp appointment requests. Propose a solution and its architecture.
a: Clarify metrics and constraints first. Then: webhook intake, queue, intent classification + RAG for FAQs, availability and booking via service layer with confirmation, human handoff, data minimisation to an approved model provider, evals, monitoring, tested backups, cost estimate, SPOFs and mitigations, phased rollout.

q: This AI-generated diff makes failing tests pass. How do you review it?
a: Read the entire diff; check for modified tests, weakened authorization/validation, new dependencies, behaviour beyond the ask; compare to the spec/permission matrix; run tests and mutate the fix; write a regression test; request explain-back.

q: How do you decide what goes into v1?
a: Tie each feature to a success criterion, estimate effort and risk, ship the smallest end-to-end flow that moves the metric, park the rest in a written v2 list.
followUps: How do you say no politely?

q: How do you prove an AI feature is ready for production?
a: Eval set with exact checks and calibrated judges including adversarial and unknown cases; pass-rate gate in CI; traces and cost per conversation; token limits; injection defences with least privilege and confirmation; monitoring and rollback of prompt/model versions.
followUps: What do you do when the eval pass rate drops after a model upgrade?
